AI read · macro regime

The macro regime is CONTRACTION at 40% confidence. That confidence level is low, so the call carries weight as a lean and loses force as a certainty.

The regime state score of 66 (TRANSITION, surveillance) points the same direction: the market is between states and tilting toward risk-off. You position for slowing growth: favor quality balance sheets and defensive exposure, and hold less in small caps and cyclicals.

Keep some dry powder, since the contrarian score of 94 says a washout entry may come. A confidence reading that rises above 40% would harden the contraction call.

A regime state score that falls back from 66 would clear the surveillance flag and reopen risk.

Cross-asset divergence radar — Cross-asset divergence watch
AI read · divergences in plain English

Divergence means two assets that normally move together are now going their own ways. Correlation drift is how far that link has loosened: a correlation of +1 means lockstep, 0 means no relationship, and -1 means mirror images.

The composite sits in the ELEVATED zone with 53.5% of 43 pairs diverging, and the mother jaws score is 100. Net bias reads -5, with 9 bearish pairs against 14 bullish.

The top pairs all score 80 (DEEP DIVERG). Semiconductors and the S&P 500 (smh_spy) slipped from +0.91 to +0.40, so chips no longer drive the index.

Momentum and the S&P (mtum_spy) fell from +0.84 to +0.27, which says the leaders have lost their grip. Copper and gold (hg_gc) went from +0.86 to -0.12, so growth and safety are pulling apart.

Gold and long bonds (gld_tlt) flipped from -0.53 to +0.66, and gold miners and gold (gdx_gld) moved from -0.25 to +0.53. Energy and tech (xle_xlk) loosened from -0.97 to -0.29.

When this many links break at once, the old market structure is giving way, and you size positions smaller until new relationships settle.

Cross-Region Surveillance
Major indices from the 4 regions/asset classes. Asia trades ahead time-wise vs US — a Tokyo overnight crash often leaks into the SPX open. Crypto = 24h leading indicator of global risk appetite.
AI read · the cross-region tape

Asia and Europe are rising while the US and crypto are falling, so the US session opens behind the rest of the world. Korea leads Asia at ^KS11 +4.6% and Germany leads Europe at ^GDAXI +3.6%, yet Hong Kong lags at ^HSI -3.4% and Switzerland, the defensive market, still gained ^SSMI +2.1%.

In the US, the Dow is down -1.5% and the Russell 2000 is down -3.4%, so the weakness sits in small caps. Crypto trades around the clock and shows the most stress: ETH-USD -11.6% and SOL-USD -14.2%.

Falling crypto alongside weak small caps says risk appetite is draining where leverage is highest. For today, expect US small caps and high beta to stay under pressure.

A rebound in crypto would be the first sign that the pressure is easing.

Crash Index — 10 lead-signal radar 5/10 · ALARM — 5+ signals aligned, action zone
AI read · volatility & crash, reconciled

The Crash Index at 5/10 and the VIX Spike tier at 1/4 disagree, and the state is coherent. The Crash Index reads price damage, breadth and cross-asset stress, so it has already crossed into the action zone.

The VIX tier reads what options traders pay for protection, and it has not moved: backwardation is off, the adaptive trigger is off, and only skew is active. The spike probability sits at 50%, a coin flip.

That combination means the market is hurting but has not panicked, and panic is the part that produces a volatility expansion. You treat the Crash Index as the early warning and the VIX tier as the trigger.

Until the tier rises above 1, you cut risk modestly instead of stepping aside fully. A move to backwardation is the signal that changes that.

Plain-English read · the Crash Index
Think of this as a smoke alarm, not a market forecast. Each of the 10 rows is a signal that led real crashes, checked over 15 years of S&P 500 history (Bonferroni-validated, so it survived a strict false-positive test). In a calm market it sits near zero by design — a low number is the alarm working, not a broken gauge. It only earns your attention when 3 or more rows light up together. Today it reads 5/10 — several signals are aligned, a real stress probability is building.

How to read
Aggregation of all panel signals across the 4 cross-asset buckets. RISK-ON = risk appetite (cyclical, equity, EM). RISK-OFF = flight to defensives (TLT, gold, JPY). Reading the table — Z-Score: number of standard deviations vs rolling 100d mean. |Z| > 2 = Kerberos entry threshold, |Z| > 2.5 = extreme (best R/R on mean-reversion). %B: position within Bollinger Bands (1.0 = upper band, 0 = lower band).

Aggregate reading — the mean of Z-scores gives a global regime indicator. Positive → cross-asset overbought market (Risk-On, watch reversal). Negative → oversold (Risk-Off, possible bottoming).
How to read
Persist = number of consecutive days above |Z| > 2.0 (Kerberos threshold). Persist ≥ 3d = validated signal (the divergence has become a regime, not a spike). Persist 1-2d = to watch. Persist 0d = dead signal. Sort on this column to find established regimes worth trading.
Glossary — 18 terms to understand the dashboard
Z-Score
Number of standard deviations vs the historical mean (rolling 100 days). Z=0 = normal level · |Z|>2 = stress · |Z|>2.5 = extreme.
Bollinger Bands
Bands drawn at ±2.2σ around a 100-day moving average. When the price exits the bands = statistically extreme signal.
Backwardation
Inverted curve: immediate fear exceeds far fear (e.g. VIX > VIX3M). Short-term panic signal.
Contango
Normal situation where far fear exceeds immediate fear. Extreme contango = complacency.
Half-life
Number of days required for a gap to the mean to halve. Measures the speed of mean-reversion.
Cointegration
Two assets that move together in the long term despite short-term fluctuations. Statistical basis of pair-trading.
Mean-reversion
Strategy betting that a gap to the mean will close. Inverse of momentum (which bets on continuation).
Breadth
Width of participation in the rally. Good breadth = many stocks rising. Bad breadth = only a few mega-caps pull the index.
Hedge ratio
Quantity of asset B to short to neutralize 1 long unit of asset A. Calculated via OLS regression on historical returns.
Lead-time
Delay between a signal's appearance and the event it predicts. Structural = 30-90d · stress = 5-30d · triggers = 1-10d.
Bonferroni
Statistical correction for multiple testing. When testing 100 signals, some seem valid by chance. Bonferroni divides the significance threshold by the number of tests to eliminate these false positives.
MCPT (Monte Carlo Permutation Test)
Robustness test: data is randomly shuffled 5000-10000 times to see if the signal appears by chance. If p < 0.05, the signal is probably real.
Walk-forward
Test where the model is trained on the first years (e.g. 2010-2020) and tested on the following years (2020-2025). Avoids in-sample overfitting.
Tail-hedge
Hedge against an extreme crash (-20% or more). Bought via deeply out-of-the-money puts. SKEW measures institutional demand for this type of insurance.
Mega-caps
The 7-10 largest market caps in the SPX (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA). Weigh ~35% of the index.
Cap-weighted vs Equal-weighted
SPY = weighted by capitalization (mega-caps dominate). RSP = each stock weighs 0.2%. Comparing both reveals concentration.
Risk parity
Portfolio strategy that balances risk (not capital) across asset classes. Stressed when stocks/bonds correlations turn positive (inflation regime).
framework rule
Fundamental principle: a solo signal = noise, 3+ aligned signals = real edge. All panel signals are Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY.
